answer: A harbor stays safe when every ship must answer a fresh signal before docking, and an agent economy can do the same: each identity faces a short, unpredictable cipher challenge once per epoch, a puzzle that only a live agent can solve inside the time window, like a relic key that fits one lock and one moment. Every extra fake identity needs another live solver watching the clock, so running a thousand clones costs a thousand attentive agents, while one honest agent answers once and keeps working.
